title: Stop Preparing and Start Proving
author: Scott D. Clary
summary: Clary argues that confidence comes through handling difficult situations, not from advance knowledge or preparation. Many aspiring leaders get stuck in a preparation loop, studying frameworks and seeking mentorship before accepting real responsibility or risk. But this delays the development of actual confidence, which only comes from proving to oneself in real time that one can manage complexity and adversity. His prescription is pragmatic: do more than you are ready for, seek stretching roles, make decisions with incomplete information, and learn from failure. Discomfort signals growth, not a need for more preparation. Leadership is proven through action.
points: Confidence is not a prerequisite but an outcome: It emerges from handling difficulty, not from knowing what to do in advance.
Preparation loops trap aspirants: Extended studying delays the only thing that builds real confidence, which is real-world action.
Discomfort is a signal to proceed: When you feel stretched and uncertain, you are in the growth zone where confidence actually develops.
The gap between readiness and action is where leadership forms: Taking on more than you are prepared for is the method, not the risk.
quotes: Confidence doesn't come from knowing what to do. Confidence comes from actually handling things when they get hard.
Most aspiring leaders spend years preparing but never actually start proving themselves. They study, plan, and delay until the moment feels perfect. That moment never comes.
The gap between who you think you are and who you actually are is proven through real decisions, real stakes, and real consequences.

You become confident not by preparing more but by doing more than you are prepared for and learning from the gap.” “Leadership is not a state of readiness. It is a practice of proving yourself in real time.” Archived from Scott's Newsletter on April 20, 2026 by Tim.
